relations.subject: server:vbucket
relations.evidence: This command lists all available vBuckets and provides information about their type: active, replica, pending or dead.

notable_absence.finding: The page asserts four possible vBucket types (active, replica, pending, dead) but the example response only ever shows 'active' and 'replica' values ('vb_100: active', 'vb_0: replica', etc.) - 'pending' and 'dead' are named in prose but never demonstrated in the sample output, so a reader has no worked example of what those two states look like in practice.

cross_component_finding: This page and cbstats-prev-vbucket.md (the very next file in this batch) are structurally near-identical: same Syntax/Description/Options/Example section order, same 'There are no options for this command' Options text, and near-identical one-sentence Description prose ('This command lists all available vBuckets and provides information about their type...' vs 'This command lists the previous state of each vBucket.') differing only in the current-vs-previous framing. That is a strong authorship-provenance signal for this round: both pages read as written in one authoring pass by the same hand, not as two independently-drafted commands that happened to converge.
cross_product_finding: cbstats is a Server-only, per-node KV-port CLI tool; Capella exposes no equivalent low-level vBucket-state inspection surface (its bucket/scope/collection concepts - capella:bucket, capella:scope, capella:collection - are documented purely through UI/REST, with no vBucket-granularity CLI at all). No cross-product concept applies here.
